correctness.rationale: The synchronous firing recurrence preserves equality of grain counts modulo \(k\) for all times, proving exact equality of lifted firing sets and full-simplex fiber inflation at each stage. Barycentric maps \(\Pi\) and \(J\) satisfy \(\Pi J=\mathrm{id}\), with \(J\Pi\) the fiber average; straight-line interpolation lies in the very same lifted simplex and gives a rotation-equivariant strong deformation retraction, uniformly in time. The zero-residue sphere and single-residue component conclusions follow directly from the small complex facet families. The proof is integral and not based on finite computations. Independent direct simulations: 450 configurations, 2270 firing-step comparisons, 192584 face comparisons, 19 \(\mathbb F_2\) Betti checks and 14 periodic-block benchmarks.

originality.rationale: The 2026 motivating article constructs avalanche complexes and persistent filtrations, but its available full text does not state the arbitrary nonnegative periodic-lift, stagewise rotation-fixed strong deformation retraction. A fully inspected published record treats a coprime-remainder (nondivisible) class, and another treats a different path-homology digraph blow-up. Neither statement implies an equivariant avalanche filtration equivalence. The central simplicial averaging is a known general technique, here used with a new exact dynamical fiber identity. Unindexed priority is a residual risk.
residual_risks: A nonindexed paper or source may have explicitly formulated the same periodic-equivariant reduction.
The barycentric averaging technique itself is elementary and is not claimed as new outside its sandpile-dynamical application.
No extension to arbitrary nonperiodic grain vectors or digraph covering maps is proved.

value.rationale: The all-time equivalence is an effective structural reduction of the newly defined persistent avalanche theory: arbitrary repetitions and unbounded nonbinary grain counts can be compressed without changing homotopy, integral homology, barcode birth/death times or the cyclic symmetry action. It proves a natural divisible-period branch of a motivating sphere prediction and distinguishes it from known nondivisible wraparound behavior. This is a general, motivated infinite-family result rather than an arbitrary finite check or an isolated small numerical improvement.
